title: Nā ʻoihana a me ke aʻo ʻana
description: Ten short stories about people learning a job: a trainee at a Hawaiian-language newspaper, a hotel housekeeper in Waikīkī, a bicycle courier in Honolulu, a law student in a courtroom, an adopted son learning to run a Maui farm, a lei-shop apprentice, a ranger at Kīlauea, a zoo keeper, an engineering student on the Waikīkī canal and two dancers training to be hula teachers.

lessons.title: Ka ʻokina ma ka nūpepa
lessons.summary: Makaleka starts training at a Hawaiian-language newspaper in Honolulu: her editor Palani finds thirteen missing ʻokina in the letters she typed, the staff chat at lunch, and her comic column about a little angel chasing the train is printed.
lessons.text:
ʻO Makaleka koʻu inoa. I kēia makahiki, ke aʻo nei au i ka hana ma kekahi nūpepa ʻōlelo Hawaiʻi ma Honolulu. Mai koʻu wā kamaliʻi mai, ua ʻiʻini au e lilo i mea kākau.

ʻO Palani ka luna hoʻoponopono o ka nūpepa. I ka lā mua, ua nīnau mai ʻo ia, "ʻO wai ka inoa ou?" Ua haʻi aku au i koʻu inoa, a ua alakaʻi ʻo ia iaʻu i kekahi pākaukau. "ʻO kēia ka noho ou, a ʻo kēia kāu kamepiula," wahi āna. "ʻO kāu hana mua, e kikokiko i kēia mau leka mai ka poʻe heluhelu. E kikokiko pono i nā ʻokina a me nā kahakō a pau."

Ua kikokiko wikiwiki au i nā leka. Ma hope o hoʻokahi hola, ua heluhelu ʻo Palani i kaʻu hana. "Maikaʻi kāu hana," wahi āna, "akā naʻe, ʻumikūmākolu ʻokina i nalowale. He hua palapala ka ʻokina. Ke nalowale ka ʻokina, loli ke ʻano o ka hua ʻōlelo, a pohihihi ka poʻe heluhelu." Ua ʻimi au i nā ʻokina ʻumikūmākolu, a ua hoʻoponopono au iā lākou a pau.

I ke ahiahi, ua walaʻau nā limahana o ka nūpepa ma ka lumi ʻaina. Ua walaʻau lākou no nā moʻolelo o ka lā. ʻAʻole au i walaʻau nui, no ka mea he malihini au.

I ka pule ʻelua, ua nīnau mai ʻo Palani, "He aha kou ʻiʻini? He aha ke ʻano moʻolelo e makemake ana ʻoe e kākau?" Ua pane au, "Makemake au e kākau i nā moʻolelo hoʻokawewae." Ua ʻae ʻo ia. "E kākau ʻoe i kekahi kolamu hoʻokawewae no ka Pōʻaono. Inā hoʻomākeʻaka kāu kolamu, e paʻi ʻia ana ia."

Ua kākau au i kekahi moʻolelo no kekahi ʻānela liʻiliʻi. Ua lele mai ka ʻānela mai ka lani mai i Honolulu, akā ʻaʻole ʻo ia i ʻike i ke kaʻaahi. Ua lele ka ʻānela ma hope o ke kaʻaahi a puni ke kūlanakauhale, a ua pau kona ikaika. Ua kikokiko mālie au i ka moʻolelo, a ua nānā au i kēlā me kēia ʻokina. Ua heluhelu ʻo Palani, a ua ʻakaʻaka nui ʻo ia. "Hoʻomākeʻaka loa kēia ʻānela!" wahi āna. "ʻAʻohe ʻokina i nalowale. E paʻi ʻia ana kāu kolamu i kēia Pōʻaono."

Nā nīnau:
He aha ka ʻiʻini o Makaleka mai kona wā kamaliʻi mai?
Ua ʻiʻini ʻo ia e lilo i mea kākau.
ʻEhia ʻokina i nalowale ma kāna hana mua?
ʻUmikūmākolu ʻokina i nalowale.
He aha ka hana a nā limahana ma ka lumi ʻaina?
Ua walaʻau lākou no nā moʻolelo o ka lā.
No wai ka moʻolelo hoʻokawewae a Makaleka?
No kekahi ʻānela liʻiliʻi i lele ma hope o ke kaʻaahi.

lessons.title: Ka lumi ʻālohilohi
lessons.summary: Haliaka begins work as a hotel housekeeper in Waikīkī; her supervisor Lokepa teaches her to open the windows, spread clean sheets, sweep the sand, wash a banana stain, close up and stand straight so her back stops hurting.
lessons.text:
He 19 makahiki o Haliaka. Ua pau kona kula kiʻekiʻe, a ua loaʻa iā ia kekahi hana ma kekahi hōkele nui ma Waikīkī. He limahana hoʻomaʻemaʻe ʻo ia. ʻO Lokepa kona luna. Ua hana ʻo Lokepa ma ka hōkele no 20 makahiki.

I ka lā mua, ua hele lāua i kekahi lumi ma ka papahele ʻumi. "Ke komo kāua i kekahi lumi," wahi a Lokepa, "e wehe mua kāua i nā pukaaniani, i komo mai ka makani." Ua wehe ʻo Haliaka i nā pukaaniani nui, a ua ʻike ʻo ia i ke kai uliuli.

ʻO ka hana ʻelua, ʻo ia ka hāliʻi ʻana i ka moena. Ua lawe aku lāua i nā kapa moena kahiko, a ua hāliʻi lāua i nā kapa keʻokeʻo hou ma luna o ka moena. "E hāliʻi pono," wahi a Lokepa. "ʻAʻole pono e waiho kekahi lepo liʻi ma ka moena."

A laila, ua lawe ʻo Haliaka i ka pulumi, a ua pulumi ʻo ia i ka papahele. Ua lawe mai nā malihini i ke one liʻi mai ke kahakai mai, no laila ua pulumi ʻo ia ma lalo o ka moena a me ka noho. Ma hope iho, ua holoi ʻo ia i ka lumi ʻauʻau, a ua holoi ʻo ia i nā pukaaniani a ʻālohilohi lākou ma ka lā.

Ma kekahi kapa keʻokeʻo, ua ʻike ʻo Haliaka i kekahi kohu ʻeleʻele. "He kohu maiʻa kēia," wahi a Lokepa. "Paʻakikī ka holoi ʻana i ke kohu maiʻa. E lawe i kēia kapa i ka lumi holoi lole." Ma mua o ko lāua haʻalele ʻana i ka lumi, ua papani ʻo Haliaka i nā pukaaniani a pau, a ua papani ʻo ia i ka puka.

I ke ahiahi, ua ʻeha ke kua o Haliaka, a ua luhi loa ʻo ia. "Luhi nō kēia hana," wahi a Lokepa. "Ke pulumi ʻoe a ke holoi ʻoe, e kū pololei ʻoe. A laila, ʻaʻole e ʻeha ana kou kua."

Ma hope o hoʻokahi mahina, ua wikiwiki ʻo Haliaka i ka hana, a ʻaʻole i ʻeha hou kona kua. I kekahi lā, ua waiho kekahi malihini i kekahi leka ma ka pākaukau: "Mahalo! ʻĀlohilohi ko mākou lumi." Ua hauʻoli loa ʻo Haliaka.

Nā nīnau:
He aha ka hana mua ke komo lāua i kekahi lumi?
Wehe mua lāua i nā pukaaniani.
He aha ka mea a Haliaka i pulumi ai ma lalo o ka moena?
Ua pulumi ʻo ia i ke one liʻi mai ke kahakai mai.
He aha ke kohu ʻeleʻele ma ke kapa keʻokeʻo?
He kohu maiʻa ia.
No ke aha i ʻeha ai ke kua o Haliaka?
Ua ʻeha kona kua no ka mea ua luhi ʻo ia i ka pulumi a me ka holoi ʻana.

lessons.title: Ka paikikala a Kaʻiwi
lessons.summary: Kaʻiwi delivers parcels by bicycle in Honolulu; one day he takes a heavy parcel inland on the train and up the valley, a downpour comes, he falls and hurts his knee, and he still delivers it before noon.
lessons.text:
He mea lawe pūʻolo ʻo Kaʻiwi ma Honolulu. Ua hoʻomaka ʻo ia i kēia hana i ka mahina i hala. ʻAʻohe ona kaʻa, no ka mea pipiʻi loa nā kaʻa a me ka ʻaila. No laila, holo ʻo ia ma kona paikikala. ʻAʻole pipiʻi ka paikikala.

I kēlā me kēia kakahiaka, hele ʻo ia i ke keʻena o ka hui. Hāʻawi kona luna, ʻo Kamanu, iā ia i nā pūʻolo o ka lā. Hoʻokomo ʻo Kaʻiwi i nā pūʻolo i loko o kekahi ʻeke nui ma kona kua. "E miki ʻoe," wahi a Kamanu. "Makemake ka poʻe e loaʻa nā pūʻolo ma mua o ke awakea." He kanaka miki ʻo Kaʻiwi.

I kekahi lā, ua loaʻa iā ia kekahi pūʻolo kaumaha no kekahi wahine e noho ana mauka loa, ma ke awāwa o Mānoa. "Lōʻihi ke ala," wahi a Kamanu. "E eʻe ʻoe i ke kaʻaahi me kou paikikala, a ma hope, e holo ʻoe mauka." Ua eʻe ʻo Kaʻiwi i ke kaʻaahi. Ua waiho ʻo ia i kona paikikala ma kahi no nā paikikala, a ua noho ʻo ia me ka pūʻolo ma kona kuli.

Ma hope o ka iho ʻana mai ke kaʻaahi mai, ua holo ʻo ia mauka. Ua ʻeleʻele ka lani, a ua hiki mai kekahi loku. Ua kahe ka wai ma ke alanui. Ma kekahi kihi, ua hina ʻo Kaʻiwi mai kona paikikala. Ua hina ʻo ia ma ke alanui pulu, a ua ʻeha kona kuli.

Ua kū hou ʻo Kaʻiwi. Ua nānā ʻo ia i ka pūʻolo. ʻAʻole i pulu ka pūʻolo, no ka mea aia ia i loko o ka ʻeke. Ua holo hou ʻo ia ma ka loku. Ua hiki ʻo ia i ka hale o ka wahine ma mua iki o ke awakea.

Ua ʻike ka wahine i kona kuli. "Ua hina ʻoe?" wahi āna. Ua hāʻawi ʻo ia iā ia i kekahi kīʻaha kī wela a me kekahi lole maloʻo. Ua pau ka loku, a ua holo ʻo Kaʻiwi i lalo i ke kūlanakauhale. I ke ahiahi, ua haʻi ʻo ia iā Kamanu. "Miki maoli ʻoe," wahi a Kamanu, "akā e mālama ʻoe iā ʻoe iho ke ua."

Nā nīnau:
No ke aha i holo ai ʻo Kaʻiwi ma ka paikikala?
No ka mea pipiʻi loa nā kaʻa a me ka ʻaila.
Makemake ka poʻe e loaʻa nā pūʻolo i ka manawa hea?
Makemake lākou e loaʻa nā pūʻolo ma mua o ke awakea.
Ua eʻe ʻo Kaʻiwi i ka aha me kona paikikala?
Ua eʻe ʻo ia i ke kaʻaahi.
He aha ka mea i loaʻa iā ia i kona hina ʻana?
Ua ʻeha kona kuli.

lessons.title: Ka ʻaha a ka lunakanawai
lessons.summary: Law student Lilinoe trains as a clerk for judge Kauhane: twelve jurors are chosen, a man suspected of stealing a car says he did not know the law, a shouting man is put out of the courtroom, and the jury convicts.
lessons.text:
He haumāna kānāwai ʻo Lilinoe ma ke kulanui. I kēia kauwela, ke hana nei ʻo ia ma ka ʻaha ma Honolulu, ma ke keʻena o ka lunakanawai ʻo Kauhane. Kākau ʻo Lilinoe i nā mea a pau i ʻōlelo ʻia ma ka ʻaha, a heluhelu ʻo ia i nā palapala no ka lunakanawai.

I kēia pule, he kalaima nui ma mua o ka ʻaha. Ua lawe ʻia kekahi kaʻa mai kekahi hale ma Kalihi, a ua hoʻohuoi nā mākaʻi i kekahi kanaka ʻōpio, ʻo Kealanahele kona inoa. Ua ʻike ʻia ʻo ia i loko o ke kaʻa i ka pō.

I ka lā mua, ua wae ʻia nā kānaka he 12, a na lākou e hoʻoholo i ka hihia. Ua nīnau ka lunakanawai i nā kānaka he nui, a ua wae ʻo ia i nā kānaka he 12. "E wae pono ʻia nā kānaka," wahi a Kauhane iā Lilinoe ma hope. "Inā ʻaʻole, ʻaʻole pololei ka ʻaha."

I ka lā ʻelua, ua kū ʻo Kealanahele i mua o ka ʻaha. "ʻAʻole au i ʻaihue," wahi āna. "Ua hāʻawi kekahi hoaaloha iaʻu i ke kaʻa. Naʻaupō au i ke kānāwai. ʻAʻole au i ʻike ua ʻaʻe au i ke kānāwai." Ua pane ka lunakanawai, "ʻAʻole hiki i ka naʻaupō ke hoʻopakele i ke kanaka. Inā ʻaʻe ke kanaka i ke kānāwai, pono ʻo ia e uku."

Ma ia manawa, ua kū kekahi kanaka ma hope o ka lumi, a ua ʻōlelo leo nui ʻo ia i ka lunakanawai. ʻAʻole ʻo ia i noho mālie, no laila ua hoʻokuke ka lunakanawai iā ia. Ua hoʻokuke ʻia ke kanaka i waho o ka ʻaha e nā kiaʻi.

Ma hope o ʻelua hola, ua hoʻi mai nā kānaka he 12. Ua ʻāhewa lākou iā Kealanahele: ua ʻaʻe ʻo ia i ke kānāwai. Ua hoʻopaʻahao ka lunakanawai iā ia no hoʻokahi makahiki.

I ke ahiahi, ua kamaʻilio ʻo Lilinoe me Kauhane. "Paʻakikī ka ʻāhewa ʻana i ke kanaka," wahi āna. "ʻAe," wahi a Kauhane. "Akā naʻe, pono ka lunakanawai e ʻonipaʻa i ke kānāwai, ʻoiai e kaumaha ana kona puʻuwai." Ua ʻōlelo ʻo Lilinoe i loko ona iho, ke lilo ʻo ia i lunakanawai, e ʻonipaʻa nō ʻo ia e like me Kauhane.

Nā nīnau:
He aha ke kalaima ma mua o ka ʻaha?
Ua lawe ʻia kekahi kaʻa mai kekahi hale ma Kalihi.
No ke aha i hoʻohuoi ai nā mākaʻi iā Kealanahele?
No ka mea ua ʻike ʻia ʻo ia i loko o ke kaʻa i ka pō.
No ke aha i hoʻokuke ai ka lunakanawai i kekahi kanaka?
ʻAʻole ʻo ia i noho mālie.
Ua hoʻopaʻahao ʻia ʻo Kealanahele no ʻehia makahiki?
Ua hoʻopaʻahao ʻia ʻo ia no hoʻokahi makahiki.

lessons.title: Ka mahiʻai ma Ulupalakua
lessons.summary: On a Maui upland farm, Kahiapo trains Kekona, the son he and his wife adopted, to run it: thorny pineapples and sour unripe ones, macadamia trees that bear after seven years, nuts packed in tins, pineapple wine, and taro boiled and pounded into poi.
lessons.text:
He mahiʻai ʻo Kahiapo ma Ulupalakua, ma ka ʻaoʻao o Haleakalā ma Maui. I ko lāua wā ʻōpio, ʻaʻohe keiki a Kahiapo a me kāna wahine, no laila ua hoʻokama lāua i kekahi keiki kāne, ʻo Kekona. Ua hoʻokama ʻia ʻo Kekona i kona makahiki ʻelua. I kēia manawa, he 20 ona makahiki, a ke aʻo nei ʻo ia i ka hana o ka mahiʻai, no ka mea ke hoʻomaha ʻo Kahiapo, nā Kekona e mālama i ka ʻāina.

Ma ka mahiʻai, kanu lākou i ka hala kahiki. Kalakala nā lau o ka hala kahiki, no laila mālama ʻo Kekona i kona mau lima. "Ua ʻeha koʻu mau lima i nā lau kalakala i koʻu wā ʻōpio," wahi a Kahiapo. "Mai ʻoki i ka hua ʻaʻole i oʻo," wahi a Kahiapo. "ʻAwaʻawa ka hua ʻaʻole i oʻo. Ke oʻo ka hua, melemele kona ʻili, a ʻono loa ia." Ua ʻoki ʻo Kekona i kekahi hua ʻōmaʻomaʻo, a ua ʻai ʻo ia i kekahi ʻāpana. ʻAwaʻawa loa! Ua ʻakaʻaka ʻo Kahiapo.

Hana lākou i ka waina mai ka hala kahiki. Hoʻokomo lākou i ka wai o nā hua oʻo i loko o nā pahu nui, a waiho lākou ia mea no kekahi mau mahina. Kūʻai aku lākou i ka waina i nā malihini.

Aia nō kekahi mau lāʻau makeima ma ka mahiʻai. "Ke kanu ʻoe i kekahi lāʻau makeima," wahi a Kahiapo, "ʻaʻole ia e hoʻohua koke. Hoʻohua ia ma hope o ʻehiku makahiki." Ke oʻo nā makeima, hāʻule lākou i ka honua. ʻOhi ʻo Kekona i nā makeima, a waiho ʻo ia iā lākou ma ka lā a maloʻo. A laila, hoʻokomo ʻo ia i nā makeima i loko o nā kini liʻiliʻi, a papani ʻo ia i nā kini. Kūʻai ʻia nā kini makeima ma Kahului.

I ka Pōʻalima, hana ka ʻohana i ka poi. Paila ʻo Kekona i ke kalo i loko o kekahi pahu hao nui no ʻekolu hola. Ma hope o ka paila ʻana, kuʻi ʻo Kahiapo a me Kekona i ke kalo me ka wai a lilo ia i poi. "Ua aʻo mai koʻu makuakāne iaʻu i ka hana poi," wahi a Kahiapo, "a i kēia manawa ke aʻo nei au iā ʻoe."

Nā nīnau:
ʻEhia makahiki o Kekona i kona hoʻokama ʻia ʻana?
He ʻelua ona makahiki i kona hoʻokama ʻia ʻana.
Pehea ka hua hala kahiki ʻaʻole i oʻo?
ʻAwaʻawa ka hua ʻaʻole i oʻo.
Hoʻohua ka lāʻau makeima ma hope o ʻehia makahiki?
Hoʻohua ia ma hope o ʻehiku makahiki.
Hoʻokomo ʻo Kekona i nā makeima i loko o ka aha?
Hoʻokomo ʻo ia iā lākou i loko o nā kini liʻiliʻi.

lessons.title: Ke kīhei kilika ʻula
lessons.summary: In Lahapa's small lei shop in Kailua, her apprentice Kalikiano strings jasmine leis and weaves lauhala; for a bride they decorate a red silk shawl, he smudges it with dirty hands and learns to wash first, and the bride and her handsome groom wear the shawl and a white shirt at the wedding.
lessons.text:
He hale kūʻai liʻi ko Lahapa ma Kailua, ma Oʻahu. Kūʻai aku ʻo ia i nā lei pua, nā pāpale lauhala a me nā ʻaʻahu āna i hana ai. I kēia makahiki, ke aʻo nei kekahi kanaka ʻōpio, ʻo Kalikiano, i ka hana ma ka hale kūʻai.

I ke kakahiaka nui, ʻohi lāua i nā pua pīkake ma ka māla ma hope o ka hale kūʻai. Liʻi a keʻokeʻo nā pua pīkake, a ʻala loa lākou. Kui lāua i nā pua pīkake i lei. "E kui mālie," wahi a Lahapa. "Palupalu nā pua pīkake." Ma hope o ke awakea, ulana lāua i ka lauhala. Ua aʻo ʻo Lahapa iā Kalikiano e ulana i kekahi pāpale lauhala, a ua hauʻoli ʻo ia i kāna pāpale mua.

I kekahi lā, ua hele mai kekahi wahine ʻōpio, ʻo Pōlani. E male ana ʻo ia ma Lāʻie i ka pule aʻe. "Makemake au i kekahi kīhei kilika no ka lā male," wahi āna. "He kilika ʻula." Ua hōʻike ʻo ia i kekahi kiʻi o kāna kāne e male ana, ʻo Kaleinani. He kanaka nohea ʻo ia. "Nohea nō kāu kāne," wahi a Lahapa. "He aha kona ʻaʻahu?" "He palaka keʻokeʻo," wahi a Pōlani. "Makemake au e kūʻai i ka palaka ma ʻaneʻi pū kekahi."

Ua noʻonoʻo ʻo Lahapa i ka hiʻona o ke kīhei: he kilika ʻula, me nā pua keʻokeʻo ma ka lihi. A laila, ua hoʻonani lāua i ke kīhei. Ua pena ʻo Lahapa i nā pua pīkake liʻi ma ka lihi o ka kilika ʻula, a ua hoʻonani ʻo Kalikiano i ka palaka me kekahi lei pīkake.

Ua lepo nā lima o Kalikiano mai ka māla, a ua kau ʻo ia i kona lima ma luna o ke kīhei. Ua kaʻe ʻo ia i ke kilika ʻula me ka lepo. "E holoi mau i kou mau lima ma mua o ka hana ʻana me ke kilika. Ke kaʻe ʻia ke kilika, paʻakikī ka holoi ʻana," wahi a Lahapa. Ua holoi mālie ʻo Lahapa i ke kīhei me ka wai anuanu, a ua nalowale ka lepo.

I ka lā male, ua komo ʻo Pōlani i ke kīhei kilika ʻula, a ua komo ʻo Kaleinani i ka palaka keʻokeʻo me ka lei pīkake. Nani ka hiʻona o lāua.

Nā nīnau:
He aha ka hana a Lahapa a me Kalikiano me nā pua pīkake?
Kui lāua i nā pua pīkake i lei.
He aha ke ʻano kīhei i makemake ai ʻo Pōlani?
Makemake ʻo ia i kekahi kīhei kilika ʻula.
He aha ka ʻaʻahu o Kaleinani?
He palaka keʻokeʻo me ka lei pīkake.
Pehea i kaʻe ai ʻo Kalikiano i ke kilika?
Ua kaʻe ʻo ia i ke kilika me kona mau lima lepo.

lessons.title: Nā nēnē o Kīlauea
lessons.summary: Hiwalani trains as a ranger at Kīlauea with Kanekoa: they count fifteen nēnē on the ash-covered land, snare rats that eat their eggs, walk into a kīpuka of old forest full of grasshoppers and worms, watch a bat at dusk, and clean a polluted pond where Hawaiian ducks live.
lessons.text:
Ke aʻo nei ʻo Hiwalani e lilo i kahu mālama ʻāina ma Kīlauea, ma ka mokupuni ʻo Hawaiʻi. ʻO Kanekoa kona kumu. Ua hana ʻo Kanekoa ma laila no 30 makahiki.

I ka lā mua, ua helu lāua i nā nēnē. He manu Hawaiʻi ka nēnē, a ʻaʻole nui nā nēnē i koe ma ka honua. Ua uhi ʻia ka ʻāina ma laila e ka lehu ʻeleʻele mai ka lua pele. Ma luna o ka lehu, ua ʻike lāua i nā nēnē he ʻumikūmālima e ʻai ana i nā lau. Ua kākau ʻo Hiwalani ma kāna puke: "ʻUmikūmālima nēnē, ma ka lehu ma ke komohana o ka lua pele."

"ʻAi nā ʻiole i nā hua o ka nēnē," wahi a Kanekoa. "No laila, kāwili mākou i nā ʻiole." Ua hōʻike ʻo ia iā Hiwalani i ke kāwili ʻana. Ua kau lāua i nā mea kāwili ma kahi e noho ai nā nēnē. Ma ke kakahiaka aʻe, ua kāwili ʻia ʻekolu ʻiole.

Ma hope, ua hele lāua i kekahi kīpuka. He kīpuka kahi o ka nahele kahiko i waena o ka pele. ʻAʻole i kahe ka pele ma luna o ke kīpuka, no laila ola mau nā lāʻau kahiko ma laila. I loko o ke kīpuka, ua ʻike ʻo Hiwalani i nā ʻūhini ma luna o nā lau a me nā ilo ma lalo o nā pōhaku. "ʻAi nā manu i nā ʻūhini a me nā ilo," wahi a Kanekoa. I ke ahiahi, ua lele kekahi peʻa ma luna o nā lāʻau o ke kīpuka. He holoholona liʻi ka peʻa, a lele ʻo ia i ka pō e ʻai i nā ʻūhini. Ua ʻoliʻoli ʻo Hiwalani i ka ʻike ʻana i ka peʻa.

I ka lā ʻelua, ua holo lāua i kekahi loko ma kahakai o Kaʻū. Noho nā koloa ma ia loko. He manu Hawaiʻi ka koloa, e like me ka nēnē. Ua haumia ka wai o ka loko i ka ʻōpala palaki a me ka ʻaila. "Ke haumia ka wai, make nā koloa," wahi a Kanekoa. Ua hōʻiliʻili lāua i ka ʻōpala a pau. Ma ka hopena o ka lā, maʻemaʻe ka wai, a hauʻoli nā koloa.

Nā nīnau:
ʻEhia nēnē i helu ʻia e Hiwalani?
Ua helu ʻo ia i nā nēnē he ʻumikūmālima.
No ke aha i kāwili ai lāua i nā ʻiole?
No ka mea ʻai nā ʻiole i nā hua o ka nēnē.
He aha ke kīpuka?
He kīpuka kahi o ka nahele kahiko i waena o ka pele.
He aha ka mea i haumia ai ka wai o ka loko?
Ua haumia ka wai i ka ʻōpala palaki a me ka ʻaila.

lessons.title: Ka iākala wīwī
lessons.summary: Lūkia starts as a keeper at the Honolulu zoo under Kamakanoe: a thin jackal gets an extra third of food, the camel's hooves are trimmed, every gate must be locked, and on New Year's night she soothes the frightened animals while the coyote runs around like mad.
lessons.text:
Ua loaʻa iā Lūkia kekahi hana hou ma ka hale holoholona ma Honolulu. He kahu holoholona ʻo ia. ʻO Kamakanoe ka mea nāna e aʻo iā ia i ka hana. I kēlā me kēia kakahiaka, hāʻawi lāua i ka ʻai i nā holoholona.

Ma ka pā mua, aia kekahi iākala mai ʻApelika mai. Wīwī loa ka iākala. "Ua hiki mai kēia iākala i ka mahina i hala," wahi a Kamakanoe. "No laila wīwī ʻo ia. E hāʻawi ʻoe iā ia i hapakolu hou aku o ka ʻai." Ua hāʻawi ʻo Lūkia i ka ʻai a me hapakolu hou aku. Ma hope o hoʻokahi mahina, ʻaʻole wīwī hou ka iākala.

Ma ka pā ʻelua, aia kekahi kaioke mai ʻAmelika mai. Ma ka pā ʻekolu, aia kekahi kāmelo me hoʻokahi kuapuʻu nui ma kona kua. Kilakila ke kāmelo ke kū ʻo ia me kona poʻo i luna. "He holoholona kilakila ʻo ia," wahi a Lūkia. "Mālama ke kuapuʻu i ka momona," wahi a Kamakanoe, "a hiki i ke kāmelo ke hele i nā lā he nui me ka ʻai ʻole."

I kēia lā, ua ʻoki ke kauka holoholona i nā maiʻao o ke kāmelo. Ua lōʻihi loa nā maiʻao, a ua ʻeha ke kāmelo i ka hele ʻana. Ua paʻa ʻo Lūkia i ke kaula o ke kāmelo, a ua ʻoki ke kauka i nā maiʻao.

Ma mua o ka haʻalele ʻana i kekahi pā, laka ʻo Kamakanoe i ka puka. "E laka mau i ka puka," wahi āna. "Akamai ke kaioke. Inā ʻaʻole i laka ʻia ka puka, e hele ʻo ia i waho." Ua laka ʻo Lūkia i kēlā me kēia puka, a ua nānā ʻo ia ʻelua manawa.

I ka pō o ka makahiki hou, ua kani nā leo nui o ka ʻahaʻaina ma ke kūlanakauhale. Ua makaʻu nā holoholona. Ua holo pupule ke kaioke a puni kona pā, a ua noho ka iākala ma hope o kekahi pōhaku. Ua noho ʻo Lūkia ma kahi kokoke i nā pā, a ua hoʻonā ʻo ia i nā holoholona me ka leo mālie. "Mai makaʻu," wahi āna. Ma hope o hoʻokahi hola, ua hoʻonā ʻia nā holoholona, a ʻaʻole i holo pupule hou ke kaioke.

Nā nīnau:
No ke aha i hāʻawi ai ʻo Lūkia i hapakolu hou aku o ka ʻai i ka iākala?
No ka mea wīwī loa ka iākala.
ʻEhia kuapuʻu ma ke kua o ke kāmelo?
Hoʻokahi kuapuʻu nui.
No ke aha i laka mau ai lāua i nā puka?
No ka mea akamai ke kaioke, a e hele ʻo ia i waho.
He aha ka hana a ke kaioke i ka pō o ka makahiki hou?
Ua holo pupule ʻo ia a puni kona pā.

lessons.title: Ka wilikī ma ke alawai
lessons.summary: Engineering student Maleko spends the summer with city engineers on the canal in Waikīkī: they measure how shallow it has become, he sees crabs and gas rising from the mud and remembers his physics, and after work he surfs, dives under a wave beside a turtle and sees a whale leap.
lessons.text:
He haumāna ʻo Maleko ma ke kulanui ma Mānoa. Ke aʻo nei ʻo ia e lilo i wilikī. Ua aʻo ʻo ia i ke kālaikūlohea no ʻelua makahiki. I kēia makahiki, ke hana nei ʻo ia me nā wilikī o ke kūlanakauhale ma ke alawai nui ma Waikīkī. ʻO Kalua kona kumu.

Ua ʻeli ʻia ke alawai 100 makahiki i hala. I kēia manawa, ua pāpaʻu ke alawai, no ka mea ua kahe mai ka lepo mai nā kahawai mauka me ka wai ua. Ua holo lāua ma ka waʻa liʻi, a ua ana lāua i ka hohonu o ka wai. Ma kekahi mau wahi, ʻaʻole i ʻoi aku ka hohonu o ka wai ma mua o hoʻokahi mika. "Pāpaʻu loa," wahi a Kalua. "Pono e ʻeli hou ʻia ke alawai."

Ma ka lihi o ke alawai, ua ʻike ʻo Maleko i nā pāpaʻi e holo ana ma ka lepo. Ke hele kokoke ka waʻa, holo nā pāpaʻi i loko o ka lepo. Ma kekahi wahi, ua like ka wai me ka wai e paila ana. "He kinoea kēlā e piʻi aʻe ana mai ka lepo," wahi a Kalua. "Hana ʻia ke kinoea e nā lau kahiko i loko o ka lepo." Ua hoʻomanaʻo ʻo Maleko i kāna papa kālaikūlohea: ʻoi aku ka māmā o ke kinoea ma mua o ka wai, no laila piʻi ke kinoea i luna.

Ma hope o ka hana, hele ʻo Maleko e heʻenalu. Ke hiki mai kekahi nalu nui, luʻu ʻo ia ma lalo o ka nalu. I kēia ahiahi, ua luʻu ʻo ia, a ua ʻike ʻo ia i kekahi honu nui ma lalo o ka wai. Ua holo mālie ka honu ma kona ʻaoʻao.

Ua noho ʻo ia ma luna o kona papa heʻenalu, a ua nānā ʻo ia i waho. Ma kahi lōʻihi, ua lele kekahi koholā i waho o ke kai. Ua hāʻule ke koholā i loko o ke kai me ka wai keʻokeʻo nui. He hoʻoilo kēia, a hele mai nā koholā i Hawaiʻi i ka hoʻoilo. Ke heʻenalu ʻo Maleko, noʻonoʻo ʻo ia i ke kālaikūlohea o nā nalu, akā i kēia ahiahi, ua noʻonoʻo wale ʻo ia i ke koholā.

Nā nīnau:
No ke aha i pāpaʻu ai ke alawai?
Ua kahe mai ka lepo mai nā kahawai mauka me ka wai ua.
He aha nā mea e holo ana ma ka lepo?
ʻO nā pāpaʻi.
No ke aha i piʻi ai ke kinoea i luna?
ʻOi aku ka māmā o ke kinoea ma mua o ka wai.
He aha ka mea a Maleko i ʻike ai i kona luʻu ʻana?
Ua ʻike ʻo ia i kekahi honu nui ma lalo o ka wai.

lessons.title: Ke Kumulipo
lessons.summary: Leimaile tells how she and her friend Kawailani train to become hula teachers under Kumu Kahoʻāno in Kāneʻohe: month by month they learn the Kumulipo, play the ʻukulele, bow and lay an offering before dancing, and finally dance with the hālau in an old stone castle in Europe.
lessons.text:
ʻO Leimaile koʻu inoa. No ʻumi makahiki, ua hula au ma ka hālau o Kumu Kahoʻāno ma Kāneʻohe. I kēia makahiki, ua koho ʻo Kumu iaʻu a me koʻu hoaaloha ʻo Kawailani e aʻo i ka hana a ke kumu hula. No laila, i kēlā me kēia Pōʻakolu, hele māua ʻo Kawailani i ka hale o Kumu, a aʻo ʻo ia iā māua.

I ka malama mua, ua hoʻomaka māua me ke Kumulipo. He mele lōʻihi loa ke Kumulipo no ka hoʻomaka ʻana o ke ao: ka pō, ke kai, nā mea ola liʻiliʻi, nā iʻa, nā manu, a hiki i ke kanaka. "ʻAʻole hiki iā ʻolua ke aʻo i ke Kumulipo a pau i hoʻokahi malama," wahi a Kumu. "E aʻo ʻolua i kekahi mau laina i kēlā me kēia lā." Ua aʻo māua i nā laina mua, a ua oli māua iā lākou i mua o Kumu.

I ka malama ʻelua, ua aʻo ʻo Kumu iā māua e hoʻokani i ka ʻukulele no nā hula ʻauana. Ua ʻeha koʻu mau lima, akā ua hoʻomaʻamaʻa au i kēlā me kēia pō. I ka pau ʻana o ka malama, ua hiki iaʻu ke hoʻokani i ʻelima mele ma ka ʻukulele.

Ua aʻo pū ʻo Kumu iā māua i nā hana ma mua o ka hula. Ma mua o ka hula ʻana, kūlou nā haumāna a pau i mua o ke kumu. A laila, kau ke kumu i kekahi mōhai i mua o ka hālau: he lei a me kekahi mau pua mai ka nahele. "ʻO ka mōhai, he mea ia e hoʻomanaʻo ai kākou i ka poʻe kahiko," wahi a Kumu. Ua kūlou māua, a ua kau māua i kā māua mōhai mua.

I ka malama ʻekolu, ua hele ka hālau a pau i ʻEulopa. Ua hula mākou ma kekahi ʻahaʻaina i loko o kekahi kākela pōhaku kahiko. Nui ke kākela, a kiʻekiʻe kona mau paia. Ua oli māua ʻo Kawailani i nā laina mua o ke Kumulipo i loko o ke kākela, a ua hula nā haumāna. Ua piha koʻu puʻuwai i ka ʻoli. Ma hope, ua ʻōlelo mai ʻo Kumu, "Ua mākaukau ʻolua." Ua ʻoli loa māua.

Nā nīnau:
He aha ka mea a Leimaile lāua ʻo Kawailani i aʻo ai i ka malama mua?
Ua aʻo lāua i ke Kumulipo.
He aha ke Kumulipo?
He mele lōʻihi loa no ka hoʻomaka ʻana o ke ao.
He aha ka hana a nā haumāna ma mua o ka hula ʻana?
Kūlou lākou i mua o ke kumu, a kau ke kumu i kekahi mōhai.
Ma hea i hula ai ka hālau ma ʻEulopa?
Ua hula lākou i loko o kekahi kākela pōhaku kahiko.
